_note: Smiff's hand-picked lists, built into /best-beer/ and /best-wine/ (linked from the pint and wine glass on the landing page). Order matters.

beer.title: Smiff's best beer in Cambridge
beer.lede: Where to go when the beer matters: real ale, craft taps, brewery taprooms and a couple of proper back-street locals.
picks: cambridge-blue
Up to 12 real ales on at once, plus regular beer festivals.
free-press
Award-winning beer in a tiny, historic back-street pub.
calverleys
Drink it where it's brewed, in the brewery's own taproom.
handsome-prince
Baron Brewing's taproom: 18 craft taps and a bottle shop.
old-ticket-office
5 hand pumps and 16 keg taps at the station, with regular tap takeovers.
pint-shop
Craft beer on Peas Hill, right in the middle of town.
elm-tree
Belgian beers in a proper back-street local.
brew-house
Beer brewed on site on King Street.
maypole
A long-standing favourite that runs its own beer festivals.
live-let-live
Real cider and a real fire.

wine.title: Smiff's best wine in Cambridge
wine.lede: Where to go for a good glass: wine bars, wine shops you can drink in, and the best wine deal in town.
picks: king-street-cellar
Smiff's favourite. An independent wine shop and bar with natural wine and craft beer.
cwm-kings-parade
Wine bar with tastings and meet-the-producer evenings.
bridge-street-wine-bar
Pick any bottle off the shelf to drink in, with outside tables.
cwm-cherry-hinton-road
A cosy neighbourhood wine bar you can book for tastings.
darrys
Upstairs wine and cocktail bar on King Street.
douce
Café, bar and hair salon in one, with wine, vinyl and books.
earl-beaconsfield
Thursday to Saturday, 5 to 8pm: buy two large glasses and get the rest of the bottle free.
